clue.text: A study adopted by group urges breakfast?

indicators.note: something adopted by a group is taken in, so these letters go inside the word for group

parts.note: a band is a musical group
to con is an old word for to study or learn
to egg someone on is to urge them

explanation.surface: A student taken on by a band whose members are pressing for their morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the dish is one example of a breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic British fried morning meal, so a fair example of breakfast, hence the query.

clue.text: American liberty? Not American high point

indicators.note: not means without, so this letter is taken out of the word for liberty

parts.note: latitude is freedom of action

explanation.surface: Is American freedom really not American at all?
explanation.definitionFit: Height above sea level, or a lofty position, is an elevated point.

clue.text: Phrase not initially a pained expression?

indicators.note: not initially means without its first letter

parts.note: to couch something is to phrase or word it

explanation.surface: A question about wording that is not, at first, a grimace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expression' looks like a face; it is an utterance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry of sudden pain is literally something said when hurt.

clue.text: Late upset for the USA involving Republican

indicators.note: involving means including, so the jumble takes in this letter
upset means knocked over, so these letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A late upset for the United States involving a Republican, like an election shock.
explanation.definitionFit: After closing time or outside normal working times, as with a late-night bar.

clue.text: Unsympathetic about each male expecting the unattainable?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outer word goes round the others

parts.note: dry can mean cold and unemotional

explanation.surface: A hard-hearted man waiting for something he can never have.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wistful and lost in fantasy hopes for what reality will not give.

clue.text: Are British, say, rearing plant with showy flowers?

indicators.note: in a down clue, rearing up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A question about whether Britons are raising a flamboyant garden plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearing' looks like growing the plant; it reverses the pieces in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The African daisy family includes a bloom with large bright daisy-like heads.

clue.text: Italy tackles rebuilding conurbation

indicators.note: rebuilding something puts it together differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Italy takes on the reconstruction of a sprawling urban area.
explanation.definitionFit: The Utah state capital is a large urban centre, a city with its suburbs.

clue.text: Nearly all nuts and fruit

indicators.note: nearly all of a word means it loses its last letter

parts.note: nuts means crazy, mad, round the bend

explanation.surface: Practically every nut plus some fruit, like a trail mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A long curved yellow tropical produce item is a typical fruit.

clue.text: What induces international to come in to face the bowling?

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so this letter goes inside the other piece

parts.note: in cricket, to bat is to face the deliveries from the bowler

explanation.surface: A cricket question: what persuades an international player to come out and bat?
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: the batter faces the bowling, so to face it is to bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lure or enticement is something that tempts or draws a target in.

clue.text: Vulgar type secures the bar, having offloaded one religious building

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the outer word holds the next one within it

parts.note: a cad is an ill-bred, ungentlemanly man
taken as written

indicators.note: offloading means getting rid of, so a letter is dropped from the piece

parts.note: a rail is a bar, as on a fence
one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A boorish drinker grabs hold of the pub bar after shedding something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like the pub; it is a RAIL, which loses its I.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's principal church is a large place of Christian worship.

clue.text: Money heading off major loss shown in production of figures on paper

parts.note: a northern British slang word for cash

indicators.note: heading off means removing the first letter

parts.note: a thrashing or heavy defeat

explanation.surface: Cash diverting a big financial loss, shown in a set of accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figures' look like numbers in a ledger; they are effigies on church memorial plaques.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying an engraved church memorial by rubbing wax over paper laid on it reproduces its figures.

clue.text: Island between river and a lake: closed area of Venice

indicators.note: the island letter sits between the river letter and the rest, inside them

parts.note: taken as written
a door that is to is shut

explanation.surface: A geography note placing an island between a river and a lake, in a shut-off part of Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: A door pushed 'to' is closed, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The district around the famous bridge over the Grand Canal is a quarter of the Italian city.

clue.text: Origin of Commonwealth: memory expertly provided by this Commonwealth leader

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, its opening letter

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory in computing
doing something well is doing it skilfully

explanation.surface: A history lesson on the Commonwealth's beginnings, skilfully recalled by the man who led it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Commonwealth here is England's republic of 1649 to 1660, not today's association of nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver, Lord Protector, headed the English republic after the execution of Charles I.

clue.text: Chance to meet clever guy going to hospital after military command

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the first one

parts.note: a parade-ground order for troops to line up
a wit is a clever, funny person

explanation.surface: A smart fellow is sent to hospital after an army order.
explanation.definitionFit: To encounter someone by accident is to bump into them by luck.

clue.text: Crack to extend, doing for flower

parts.note: a snap is a sharp crack
to drag on is to go on far too long

explanation.surface: A crack spreading until it kills off a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing for' looks like 'killing'; it is a link meaning 'serving as'.
explanation.definitionFit: Antirrhinum, the garden bloom whose petals open like a jaw, has this common name.

clue.text: Support ditching leader in speech

indicators.note: ditching the leader drops the opening letter of the word for support

parts.note: a plant's stem or shaft that holds up a flower or leaf

explanation.surface: Backers abandon their chief in an address.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech is spoken language or conversation, a chat or discourse.

clue.text: Maiden with a sexy persona picked up song — it's the drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the letters so they read upwards

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for maiden over
taken as written
it is sex appeal, as in the It girl
an aria is an operatic song

explanation.surface: A girl with a seductive image takes up a song, and the drink is to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jamaican coffee liqueur sold under this brand name is an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Inclination Conservative has to avoid restraint

indicators.note: avoiding the letter means it is left out of the longer word

parts.note: a cramp is a clamping device, hence something that confines

explanation.surface: A Tory leaning that must steer clear of curbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope or incline, such as one used by wheelchairs, is a literal inclination.

clue.text: Starts to run off couple of chapters bound in product of cow (leather)

indicators.note: bound in means enclosed, so these letters sit inside the cow word

parts.note: moo is the sound a cow produces

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

parts.note: C is chapter, so two of them are CC

explanation.surface: A bookbinder's note: a couple of chapters bound in cowhide, the leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'product of cow' looks like hide; it is the cow's sound, MOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine goatskin used for bookbinding is a type of tanned hide.

clue.text: Working for another redefinition of ritual, getting lot of criticism

indicators.note: a redefinition recasts something, so these letters are reworked
a lot of, not all, means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: stick is informal for harsh criticism, as in getting stick

explanation.surface: A revamped ceremony meets with heavy disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redefinition of' rearranges RITUAL to ALTRUI; STICK loses its K.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfless conduct is acting for the good of others rather than oneself.

clue.text: Drunk fairly good after swallowing quantity of drink?

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so the outer word encloses the other

parts.note: a tidy sum is a fairly good one
DL is a decilitre, a measure of liquid

explanation.surface: Merrily tipsy after downing a decent amount of booze.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly tipsy, a British informal word for mildly intoxicated.

clue.text: Suppress encouragement to speed — it isn't necessary

indicators.note: something unnecessary can be dropped, so this word is removed

parts.note: an urging to hurry, telling a driver to floor the accelerator

explanation.surface: Urging a driver to hurry, then saying there is no need.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush or squash, as trampling underfoot, is to suppress.

clue.text: Not quite every item about it will identify singer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outer phrase goes round this word

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one, which is not quite every
one is a single item or unit

explanation.surface: An inventory that is almost complete will reveal who the vocalist is.
explanation.definitionFit: A male voice between tenor and bass, and so a vocalist of that range.

clue.text: Absorbed by a film about Germany

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means around, so the film word wraps the country letter

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on glass
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Engrossed in a movie set in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Being among or surrounded by something is being taken in or engulfed by it.

clue.text: Rising profits, ignoring current problem

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out this letter
in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: gains are profits
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Profits going up while overlooking the present difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'present'; it is the physics symbol I.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch or unexpected obstacle is a difficulty.

clue.text: Start one new plan, swindle having failed

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: a failed swindle has disappeared, so those letters drop out

parts.note: a conception is an idea or design
a con is a swindle

explanation.surface: Begin with a fresh scheme after a fraud has collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: The beginning or founding of an enterprise is its starting point.

clue.text: Bank response ignoring pence

indicators.note: ignoring the letter means it is left out

parts.note: a reply is a response

explanation.surface: A bank's answer that disregards the small change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is a verb here, as in 'bank on', not a lender.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on someone is to depend or count on them.

clue.text: Reason to monopolise light in film

parts.note: grounds are reasons, as in grounds for complaint
to hog is to keep all to oneself
day is daylight, the light hours

explanation.surface: A motive for hogging the lighting in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1993 Bill Murray comedy about a weatherman reliving one February day.
